notes.text: The opening continuation says that the topological Teichmüller groupoid leads to structures whose cutting circles are effectively marked, while one still wants the right to forget those markings. Section D introduces recollement. It specifies a part A′ of the free-edge set A_l and a fixed-point-free involution, described parenthetically by equivalence classes of cardinality 2. For each pair it asks for orientation-reversing isomorphisms between C_a and C_a′ that are inverse to one another. The sentence about determination up to unique isomorphism stops at unique on this page. These are statements read from the page, not proof claims.

The source reads tout orbite, un isom. and l’un; these endings have not been adjusted for agreement. The last isom has no point, although the preceding un isom. does. No continuation such as près is supplied after the page-ending unique.

The visible {c,c′} pair is not crossed by an independent strike. The raised A′ and the curved attachment marks may indicate replacement, but that intention does not erase the visible pair. The first alternative therefore retains it live. The de after orbite receives the same treatment because its curved overhead line does not independently strike the letters. Both state questions are reserved for independent audit.

The original and each prepared half were read once, including witness agreements. Nineteen first-pass crops were viewed. The extra groupoid_name crop checked the agreed first-line proper name and accents without changing the reading. No OCR, outside page packet, web lookup, TeX compilation or blind second reading was used. Page-specific generators and working files are retained.

The independent TSV was frozen before comparison, and all ten unequal boxes were viewed. The two cancelled formulas retain STD and the short et les sigma fragment: the cancellation rule has no independent arrowhead. The old item-b index remains 2/l, with no securely distinct quotient slash or pi. The c,c-prime pair remains different in glyph from the later a,a-prime pair; no mathematical regularization was made. The d-equiv ending is now recorded as a doubtful abbreviation. The final a-grave/colon and singular/plural endings remain explicit uncertainties.
